text:
Samir: seeing a short ECC spike on us-west1-pool-3 starting ~1749998800, multiple jobs hitting Xid 65 and a few OOMs. Not sure if it's noisy cards or a transient fan issue.
Priya: noted, any correlate with temperature or power rails?
Samir: temps look normal in the last 2h, nvml reports a handful of cards with small but growing correctable counts. aggregate ecc rate ~0.9 errs/min for the pool for the 5m window.
Alex: can you paste the query you ran?
Samir: fetch from graphite: `sumSeries(ecc.correctables.count.us-west1-pool-3.*.5m)` and per-card: `aliasByNode(ecc.correctables.count.*,3)`
Jenna: looking at per-card series now — 3 cards are ~2-3x baseline, others at 0.1x. one card (card-12) has bursty spikes.
Mateo: what's our current soft-drain policy threshold? I recall something like 1.5 errs/min sustained 3m or a burst >50 in a minute.
Priya: policy doc: soft-drain if moving_avg(5m) > 1.2 and burst(1m) > 30, but we recently relaxed thresholds for APAC pools.
Samir: right — this pool is high-util and draining would knock production latency. we need cost-aware decision: avoid mass drains.
Alex: proposal: introduce a confidence score that weights moving_avg, burstiness (stddev), and concurrent Xid counts. If score > 0.8 trigger soft-drain; between 0.5-0.8 send alert + recheck 10m later.
Jenna: agree. quick heuristic: score = sigmoid(0.6*norm_avg + 0.3*norm_burst + 0.1*xid_ratio). We can normalize against 90th-percentile baseline per-card.
Mateo: practical ask — can we run a dry-run that marks cards as candidates but doesn't evict jobs, then simulate capacity impact? I can run the scheduler sim.
Samir: yes please. also want a temporary mitigation path: `node-restart` of mdev driver and skip full evacuation unless score >0.9.
Priya: infra-bot: created incident INC-2026-2347 for us-west1 pool noisy-cards. tagging ENG-SRE and ENG-INFRA. :rotating_light:
infra-bot: monitoring: added a 10m suppression to avoid alert storms while we triage.
Alex: can we get a quick cost estimate if we soft-drain 3 GPUs for 1h? ballpark?
Mateo: rough calc: 3 cards * 4 tokens/sec workload * 3600s * $0.000003 per token ~ $0.13 — negligible. bigger cost is capacity headroom triggering oversubscribe or falling back to lower-tier models.
Jenna: alternative: apply per-card kernel-retry bump and disable aggressive preemption to reduce job failures until we decide. lower-risk.
Samir: action items: 1) Mateo to run scheduler sim with candidate list (ETA 20m). 2) Alex to add confidence-score metric and a 10m re-eval window. 3) Jenna to apply kernel retry bump on card-12. 4) Priya to watch temp/power for next 30m.
Priya: noted, will also check recent BIOS/firmware rollout logs for that rack.
Mateo: sim results: evicting top-3 noisy cards increases latency SLO risk from 0.3% -> 0.9% for 15m spike. we probably shouldn't auto-evict at score 0.8.
Alex: updated rule: auto soft-drain threshold -> score >= 0.92 AND predicted SLO impact < 0.5%. otherwise create `noisy-card` remediation ticket and escalate.
Samir: good compromise. I'll run an immediate manual soft-drain on card-12 for 15m and monitor.
infra-bot: action log: manual-soft-drain started on us-west1-pool-3/card-12 by Samir at 1749999125.
Jenna: keeping an eye on retries, no new Xids on card-12 in last 4m.
Priya: firmware rollback on rack-7 at 1749999000 matches start of spike — filing note.
Samir: final note — let's add the following to runbook: prefer confidence-score + predicted SLO sim before any auto-evict. defer auto-drain unless both conditions satisfied.
Alex: will PR the runbook change and add a dashboard for confidence score.
Mateo: sim complete; posting results in ENG-SRE runbook thread.
Samir: thanks all, closing triage for now. will reopen if score rises. :thumbsup:
